narrativeBlocks.title: The feather that starts it
narrativeBlocks.body: A tsar covets the Firebird — the glowing bird that comes to steal his golden apples. His youngest son Ivan goes to catch it and finds only a feather — but a feather so bright it lights the room.

narrativeBlocks.title: The wolf who eats his horse
narrativeBlocks.body: On the road a grey wolf eats Ivan's horse — then, in compensation, becomes his guide and mount: faster than any horse, wiser than any courtier, and the architect of every success Ivan has.

narrativeBlocks.title: Demands that multiply
narrativeBlocks.body: Each prize breeds a new demand: the Firebird requires a golden cage; the beautiful princess requires another princess's hand in exchange; each errand to a new tsar spirals. The quest teaches that getting is never the end.

narrativeBlocks.title: The wolf makes it work
narrativeBlocks.body: Through every snag, the wolf's counsel rescues Ivan — impersonating him, advising his refusals, turning each 'impossible' exchange around. The hero's real strength is that he listens to the wolf.

narrativeBlocks.title: A chapbook's reach
narrativeBlocks.body: The Firebird tale survived in cheap printed chapbooks — folk publishing that carried the stories to generations. The tale's structure — radiant prize, wise animal guide, cascading demands — is one of the world's most copied quest-patterns.
